title: Organized Crime and Firms: Evidence from Antimafia Enforcement Actions
eligible_reason: Binary absorbing treatment (Shocked_Already at municipality level; dummy_confiscation at firm level, lagged one year) switching on at municipality-specific first-confiscation years, 1995-2013 (19 cohorts per Figure 2b data: 87 municipalities first treated in 1995 rising to 621 cumulative by 2013; ~7,300 never treated), estimated by static TWFE with municipality (or firm) FE and province x year (or industry x province x year) FE, no controls, clustered by municipality. Panel A of Tables 3, 4, 5, 9 (municipality) and Table 6 (firm) contain 15 qualifying columns. Panel B tables and Figures 5-7 are stacked (excluded).
design_notes: Stata (reghdfe, gegen). Muni_Level.do: Tables 1A, 1C, 2A-C, 3A/B, 4A/B, 5A/B, 9A/B, Figures 1-6. Firm_Level.do: Tables 1B, 6A/B, 7A/B, 8A/B, Figure 7. Province x year FE (ProvYear/ProvYe = group(nuts3 year)) is a time-invariant characteristic x time FE (allowed). Firm specs use L.dummy_confiscation with tsset firm_id year. Original_Results/*.csv hold the published tables (coefficients and t-stats) and Original_Log_Files/*.smcl the full original Stata logs, so published estimates are recoverable. Modified_Data: Muni_panel.dta (94,953 muni-years, 4,628 ids, 1990-2015) with outcomes shuffled via shufflevar - and Shocked_Already is also scrambled (only 17% of municipalities have a monotone path; 7,650 switch-offs), so even treatment timing is unusable at the muni level; firm_panel.dta (809,137 firm-years, 122,560 firms = 1/12 sample) keeps real treatment timing (first_confisc_year 1996-2013, 18 cohorts; 53,955 never-treated firms; dummy_confiscation absorbing) but accounting outcomes are random draws.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: From Modified_Data/Data_by_year.dta (Figure 2b): municipalities first treated each year 1995-2013 (87, 62, 44, 31, 36, 29, 39, 46, 38, 20, 29, 17, 29, 27, 29, 24, 19, 8, 7; cumulative 621). Firm-level cohorts 1996-2013 (first_confisc_year in firm_panel.dta).
always_treated_note: Some municipalities were first shocked before 1995 (FirstShock values 1982-1994 in data) and intimidation/auction subsamples (2010-2015, 2007-2015) contain many municipalities already treated at window start.
modern_estimators_named: stacked regression (Cengiz et al. 2019 style) as robustness in Panel B

data_access: proprietary (Orbis/Bureau van Dijk); package ships modified pseudo-data only
data_files: Modified_Data/Muni_panel.dta (12.8 MB; outcomes and treatment shuffled)
Modified_Data/firm_panel.dta (48.6 MB; 1/12 firms, synthetic accounting variables, real treatment timing)
replication_feasible: no (requires original data from authors; pseudo-data cannot reproduce any estimate)
screener_notes: Readme.docx states muni outcomes were modified with shufflevar; my check shows Shocked_Already is also non-monotone in Muni_panel.dta, so cohort counts from that file (4,055 'ever shocked' of 4,628) are artefacts; use Data_by_year.dta (621 ever-treated municipalities) instead. Muni-level regression sample has ~3,850 municipalities per year (N=80,800 over 21 years). Published estimates are also in Original_Log_Files/*.smcl for SEs. Auction, intimidation and municipal-budget outcomes may come from public Italian sources, but they were shuffled in the package too.
